findings.situation: A filer receiving SSDI for injuries caused directly by a terrorist attack, such as the September 11 firefighter in the instructions' example, has box 5 of their SSA-1099 showing all benefits, including the excludable part.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 31: "Don't include in your income any disability payments (including Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) payments) you receive for injuries incurred as a direct result of a terrorist attack ... If these payments are incorrectly reported as taxable on Form SSA-1099, don't include the nontaxable portion of income on your tax return ... you can exclude only 4 months ... ($6,000). You must report the remaining $12,000 on line 6a."
findings.why: The question asks for the plain "Total of box 5 (net benefits) of all your Forms SSA-1099 and RRB-1099". A truthful answer would be $18,000 in the example, but worksheet line 1 and line 6a must hold only the $12,000 that is not excluded. Nothing in the help or the listed refusals removes the excludable portion.

findings.situation: A married couple filing jointly where both spouses received Forms SSA-1099 or RRB-1099.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 32, worksheet line 8: "Married filing jointly, enter $32,000"; line 1: "Enter the total amount from box 5 of all your Forms SSA-1099 and RRB-1099"
findings.why: On a joint return, line 1 must include both spouses' box 5 amounts. An ordinary filer answering a question addressed to "your" forms could reasonably enter only their own forms. Nothing in the help says to include the spouse's forms.

locators: p. 32, Social Security Benefits Worksheet, line 1
p. 32, Social Security Benefits Worksheet, line 1; p. 31, Lines 6a and 6b

findings.situation: A single, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse, or joint filer must still give a yes or no, and could reasonably answer either 'yes' (no spouse lived with them) or 'no' (not applicable); the helpers ssb.mfs_base and ssb.mfs_adjust use that answer without checking filing status.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 32, line 8: "Single, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse, or married filing separately and you lived apart from your spouse for all of 2025, enter $25,000"; question: "If you are married filing separately: did you live apart from your spouse for all of 2025?"
findings.why: The question only applies to married filing separately filers, but it accepts only yes or no and gives no 'not applicable' choice. A non-MFS filer's answer therefore changes which $25,000 and $9,000 helper amounts are produced. If lines 8 and 10 combine these helpers with the filing-status amounts, the result could be wrong or counted twice. The help text, which says married filing separately is refused, adds to the confusion for MFS filers.

locators: p. 31, Line 6d; p. 32, worksheet, Before you begin and line 8
